source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

## 审查报告 — plan-011 (Rule-Based Routing Baseline)

**结论**: PASS

### 发现

- [severity: info] **v1 关键词集（20词，含通用动词）结构性退化为 always-det**：匹配率 86.13%，其中 "connect" 一词贡献 3963 次命中，远超其他关键词。对 det-preferred 类别的 precision 仅 0.42，说明高匹配率来自关键词过于宽泛，而非真正识别了路由信号。这本质上等价于 always-deterministic baseline。

- [severity: info] **v2 关键词集（17词，仅科学术语）结构性退化为 always-internal**：匹配率仅 4.94%，accuracy 1.19%。科学专有词在 action 文本中极少出现，导致几乎所有 step 都 fallback 到 internal，等价于 always-internal baseline。

- [severity: info] **两套关键词均预注册于 src/rule_based_keywords.json**，实验流程合规，无事后调参嫌疑。

- [severity: info] **结论与 D014 决策一致**：关键词路由在 ScienceWorld 上结构性失败——宽泛词退化为 always-det，窄义词退化为 always-internal，不存在"恰好对"的中间地带。这为论文提供了有力的 negative baseline：rule-based 方法无法捕捉路由信号，支持 episode-level counterfactual 方法论的必要性论证。

### 建议

- 论文中报告此结果时建议同时呈现 v1 和 v2，展示关键词粒度谱上的两极退化模式（too broad → always-det; too narrow → always-internal），比只报一个版本更有说服力。

No 2025-2026 paper claims death/safety avoidance\\n# as the dominant routing signal in LLM agent systems.\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# CATEGORY: ScienceWorld Agent Baselines (must-cite)\\n# ============================================================\\nscienceworld_baselines:\\n  - id: cogrouter-2026\\n    title: \\\"Think Fast and Slow: Step-Level Cognitive Depth Adaptation for LLM Agents\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Yang et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2602.12662, Feb 2026\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: high\\n    summary: >\\n      SOTA on ScienceWorld (82.3% with Qwen2.5-7B). Routes between cognitive\\n      depth levels (instinct to strategic planning) via CoPO, not between\\n      internal vs deterministic computation. Does not analyze WHAT drives\\n      routing signal. Cite as SOTA baseline and adaptive computation related work.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      CogRouter optimizes HOW MUCH to think; we analyze WHAT routing learns\\n      (death avoidance = 99%). Different routing dimensions (depth vs modality).\\n\\n  - id: itp-2026\\n    title: \\\"Imagine-then-Plan: Agent Learning from Adaptive Lookahead with World Models\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Liu et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2601.08955, Jan 2026\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: high\\n    summary: >\\n      Extends POIMDP with world model lookahead on ScienceWorld/ALFWorld/WebShop.\\n      Adaptive lookahead horizon based on task progress. Uses approximate LLM\\n      world model, not deterministic simulator.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      ITP routes lookahead depth using world model; we route modality (internal\\n      vs deterministic) and discover death avoidance dominates. ITP world\\n      model is approximate; our deterministic computation is exact.\\n\\n  - id: mtrouter-2026\\n    title: \\\"MTRouter: Cost-Aware Multi-Turn LLM Routing with History-Model Joint Embeddings\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Zhang et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2604.23530, ACL 2026\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: high\\n    summary: >\\n      Multi-turn routing between different LLMs on ScienceWorld (53.8 avg score,\\n      -58.7% cost vs GPT-5). Routes between model APIs for cost optimization.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      MTRouter routes between different LLMs (cost-quality tradeoff); we route\\n      between reasoning modalities (internal vs deterministic). Different routing\\n      targets, different findings. We analyze routing signal composition;\\n      they optimize cost.\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# CATEGORY: Tool-Use Routing & Learning (positioning)\\n# ============================================================\\ntool_use_routing:\\n  - id: retool-2026\\n    title: \\\"ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Feng et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2504.11536, ICLR 2026\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: high\\n    summary: >\\n      RL framework to learn when to invoke code interpreter for math reasoning.\\n      Implicit routing entangled with backbone LLM. AIME2024 67.0% (Qwen2.5-32B).\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      ReTool implicit routing via RL in math domain. SimGate explicit modular\\n      router with counterfactual labels in interactive environment. We analyze\\n      routing signal composition; they optimize tool usage strategy.\\n\\n  - id: toolformer-2024\\n    title: \\\"Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Schick et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"NeurIPS 2024\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: Self-supervised tool-use learning via API call insertion.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      Hindsight labels from environment forking, not self-supervised. Safety-aware\\n      framing, not general tool selection.\\n\\n  - id: art-2023\\n    title: \\\"ART: Automatic Multi-step Reasoning and Tool-use for Large Language Models\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Paranjape et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"2023\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: Automated tool selection via LLM reasoning chains.\\n    our_differentiation: Dedicated lightweight router, not LLM-as-router.\\n\\n  - id: chameleon-2024\\n    title: \\\"Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Lu et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"2024\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: LLM-as-planner routing to diverse tools.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      Single modality (deterministic computation), explicit small router, counterfactual\\n      methodology to understand routing signal composition.\\n\\n  - id: toolkengpt-2024\\n    title: \\\"ToolkenGPT: Augmenting Frozen Language Models with Massive Tools via Tool Embeddings\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Hao et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"2024\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: low\\n    summary: Token-level tool triggers via special embeddings.\\n    our_differentiation: Step-level routing with counterfactual episode labels.\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# CATEGORY: Adaptive Computation & Reasoning Depth\\n# ============================================================\\nadaptive_computation:\\n  - id: ares-2026\\n    title: \\\"ARES: Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection for Efficient LLM Agents\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Yang et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2603.07915, Mar 2026\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: >\\n      Lightweight router predicts per-step reasoning effort (low/medium/high).\\n      Trained via trajectory filtering + effort annotation + SFT. Reduces tokens\\n      by 52.7%. Evaluated on TAU-Bench, WebArena, BrowseComp-Plus.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      Similar router architecture pattern (lightweight SFT router), but routes\\n      reasoning effort, not modality. We contribute the empirical finding about\\n      death avoidance dominance, not the router design.\\n\\n  - id: dynathink-2025\\n    title: \\\"Dyna-Think: Synergizing Reasoning, Acting, and World Model Simulation in AI Agents\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2506.00320, May 2025\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: >\\n      Integrates world model simulation into agent reasoning loop. Uses critique\\n      generation for world model training. 32B Dyna-Think matches 685B R1 with\\n      2x fewer tokens.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      Dyna-Think synthesizes reasoning and simulation; we analyze the signal\\n      composition of routing between them and find death avoidance dominates.\\n\\n  - id: mixture-of-recursions-2025\\n    title: \\\"Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation\\\"\\n    authors: \\\"Bae et al.\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2507.10524, NeurIPS 2025\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: low\\n    summary: Architecture-level adaptive depth routing via lightweight routers.\\n    our_differentiation: Architecture-level, not agent-level routing.\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# CATEGORY: Agent Safety & Failure Analysis\\n# ============================================================\\nagent_safety:\\n  - id: toolsafety-2025\\n    title: \\\"ToolSafety: A Comprehensive Dataset for Enhancing Safety in LLM-Based Agent Tool Invocations\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"EMNLP 2025\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: >\\n      5668 direct harm + 4311 indirect harm + 4311 multi-step samples for tool\\n      invocation safety. We study\\n      safety as catastrophic task failure (death) and its role as routing signal.\\n      Different safety definitions.\\n\\n  - id: openagentsafety-2026\\n    title: \\\"OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Benchmark\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"ICLR 2026\\\"\\n    relation: background\\n    relevance: low\\n    summary: >\\n      Agent safety benchmark. Finds individually safe steps compounding into\\n      unsafe outcomes over multi-turn interactions.\\n\\n  - id: llm-agentic-failures-2025\\n    title: \\\"How Do LLMs Fail In Agentic Scenarios? A Qualitative Analysis\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"arXiv:2512.07497, Dec 2025\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: medium\\n    summary: >\\n      Identifies 4 failure archetypes: premature action, over-helpfulness,\\n      distractor pollution, fragile execution. Qualitative analysis on 900 traces.\\n    our_differentiation: >\\n      They categorize failure types qualitatively; we quantify the dominant\\n      failure mechanism (death) and its contribution to routing signal (99%).\\n\\n  - id: envsimbench-2025\\n    title: \\\"EnvSimBench: State Prediction for LLM Environment Simulation\\\"\\n    venue: \\\"2025\\\"\\n    relation: complementary\\n    relevance: high\\n    summary: >\\n      Discovers state-change cliff: LLMs fail catastrophically when multiple\\n      state variables require simultaneous updates.    - Mitigation: Short paper format justifies focused evaluation. ScienceWorld uniquely tests rule-governed dynamics with catastrophic penalties. Discuss MATH/API extension as future work.

3. **"Comparison unfair — CogRouter uses RL (CoPO), you use SFT"**
   - Mitigation: Our primary comparison is SimGate vs ablated baselines (always-internal, always-deterministic, random, heuristic) — all same training budget. CogRouter/ITP-R cited from papers for context.

4. **"Death avoidance is trivial — just always use deterministic"**
   - Mitigation: We do NOT claim selective > unconditional deterministic. Our contribution is the empirical finding that death avoidance dominates routing signal (~99%), and the methodology that reveals this. Always-deterministic is a strong baseline — the interesting question is WHY (death avoidance), not WHETHER to route selectively. Plan-011 rule-based comparison + plan-012 death decomposition quantify this.

5. **"DAgger gap — SFT on pure-strategy trajectories may not transfer to mixed-strategy deployment"**
   - Mitigation: Acknowledge explicitly (cite Ross et al. 2011). Plan C exacerbates this: router trains on always-internal/always-deterministic trajectories but deploys on mixed. Report train/test gap. If significant, discuss DAgger-style iterative relabeling as extension. Note: Plan C's episode-level labels avoid oracle circularity (no per-step tie-breaking), which is a methodological advantage even if distribution shift remains.

6. **"ScienceWorld's -100 penalty inflates gains"** (Dream all 3 tiers)
   - Mitigation: Report gains WITH and WITHOUT death episodes separately. If non-death gains are small, honestly acknowledge that the primary value is catastrophic failure prevention — this IS our framing. Also report: what fraction of routing labels are genuine vs tie-break artifacts.

7. **"Missing tool-use literature — this is just Toolformer"** (Dream all 3 tiers, CRITICAL)
   - Mitigation: Dedicated Related Work section. Position against Toolformer/ART/Chameleon. Differentiation: counterfactual trajectory labeling (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection), explicit modular router (not LLM-as-router).

8. **"Rule-based routing baseline missing"** (Dream median + worst)
   - Mitigation: **D014 resolved — keyword routing structurally fails.** Two keyword lists tested: v1 (generic verbs incl. connect) → ≈always-det (85.8%); v2 (science-only: heat/boil/melt/freeze) → ≈always-internal (4.9%, near-zero hits). ScienceWorld actions use generic interaction verbs, not science keywords. Paper positions this as "structural failure analysis" — keyword heuristics fundamentally cannot capture routing signal in this environment, supporting the need for learned/observation-based approaches. D014: keywords v2 (science-only verbs), v1 had connect/disconnect degeneracy.

- Short paper format matches focused contribution scope
- Risk: Reviewer may expect ALFWorld evaluation (standard agent benchmark pair) — address in "Scope & Future Work" paragraph
- Risk: "Death avoidance is the only signal" may seem like a limited finding — mitigate by framing as "this IS the insight" (most routing literature assumes diverse routing benefits; we show it's dominated by one mechanism) + diagnostic methodology has value beyond ScienceWorld
- Risk: Router ≈ always-det ≈ rule-based keyword heuristic → novelty concern. **D014 update: keyword routing structurally fails on ScienceWorld** — v1 (generic verbs) ≈ always-det (85.8%), v2 (science keywords) ≈ always-internal (4.9%). ScienceWorld actions use generic interaction verbs (connect/move/pick up), not science-specific keywords, so no keyword list provides meaningful routing. This is a POSITIVE finding: positions keyword routing as "structural failure analysis" in the paper, strengthens case for learned routing or observation-based approaches.

1. **Scope narrowed**: IDEA_BRIEF proposed 3 tracks (ScienceWorld + ALFWorld + MATH). Short paper focuses on ScienceWorld only in main text; MATH as P1 extension; ALFWorld deferred.
2. **Framing shifted**: From "general routing to deterministic computation" to "safety-aware routing" based on MVP death avoidance finding.
3. **Claims reduced**: From 4 hypotheses (H1-H4) to 2 focused claims (C1-C2).

## 决策记录

### plan-011 已关闭 (2026-05-13)
Director 决策：接受 keywords v1 (always-det) + v2 (always-internal) 结果，不设计第三种 heuristic。
定位为论文 "structural failure analysis"——keyword routing 在 ScienceWorld episode-level 结构性失效。

### plan-001b blocking gate (2026-05-13)
4 项检查全部通过：pipeline-format-fix ✅, dry-run ✅, episodes.jsonl ✅, classify_episode_labels() 三标签 ✅

### D013 framing pivot (2026-05-13)
核心方向：death avoidance dominates routing signal (~99%)。
论文贡献 = empirical finding + counterfactual methodology，非 router 架构。
实测数据：Δ_full=+38.33, Δ_nd=+0.48, r=0.986 p<0.0001 (30 tasks, 249 episodes)。

### 预筛最终结果 (2026-05-13, 25/25 tasks)
- death-dominated: 19, genuine-det: 5, internal-preferred: 1
- Genuine-det (DAF < 95%): measure-melting-point-unknown (59.4%), find-living-thing (89.2%), find-plant (93.5%), find-non-living-thing (0%, int-preferred)
- 注意：DAF 分类与原始 Δ_nd > +3 分类有差异，plan-001b 完整数据后需重新评估

### GPU 负载均衡计划 (2026-05-14)
Director 指令：GPU1 完成当前 4 tasks + find-non-living-thing extra 20 eps 后，接管 GPU0 剩余未开始的 2 个 tasks。

提交 Director 决策。推荐档位 B："Death avoidance ~99% of routing signal, non-death deltas small and inconsistent"。
- 档 A "唯一机制"：最强但 find-animal +4.2 可能反例
- 档 B "主导+negligible"：稳健，当前数据已支持（推荐）
- 档 C "主要机制"：最保守，novelty 可能不够

### 文献扫描结果 (2026-05-14)
12 篇新论文扫描，**无 direct competitor，novelty confirmed**。
- 关键定位论文：CogRouter (ScienceWorld SOTA 82.3%), ReTool (ICLR 2026 tool-use), MTRouter (ACL 2026 multi-turn), ITP (世界模型)
- 重要发现：EnvSimBench 的 "state-change cliff" 现象为我们的 death avoidance 发现提供底层机制解释
- 差异化：现有工作路由不同目标（认知深度/不同LLM/推理强度），无人分析 routing signal 的组成（death vs non-death）

# Related Work — Draft v1

\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Tool-Use Learning.}
A line of work teaches LLMs when and how to invoke external tools.
Toolformer \cite{toolformer-2024} inserts API calls via self-supervised filtering, while ART \cite{art-2023} uses LLM reasoning chains to select tools automatically, and Chameleon \cite{chameleon-2024} composes diverse tool modules under LLM-as-planner orchestration.
More recently, ReTool \cite{retool-2026} applies reinforcement learning to learn implicit code-interpreter invocation strategies for mathematical reasoning.
Our work differs along three axes: (1) we generate routing labels via \emph{episode-level counterfactual analysis}---running complete trajectories under competing strategies---rather than self-supervised or RL-based signals; (2) we frame routing as \emph{catastrophic failure prevention} rather than general tool selection; and (3) we train an explicit lightweight router decoupled from the backbone LLM, enabling diagnostic analysis of what the routing signal encodes.

\paragraph{Adaptive Computation.}
Several recent methods adapt reasoning effort per step.
CogRouter \cite{cogrouter-2026} achieves 82.3\% on ScienceWorld by routing among cognitive depth levels (instinct to strategic planning) via Cooperative Policy Optimization, while ARES \cite{ares-2026} trains a lightweight router to select per-step reasoning effort (low/medium/high), reducing token cost by 52.7\%.
Mixture-of-Recursions \cite{mixture-of-recursions-2025} applies adaptive depth at the architecture level via per-token recursive routing.
These methods route \emph{how much} to reason; we route \emph{which modality} to use (internal LLM reasoning vs.\ deterministic computation) and contribute the empirical finding that death avoidance accounts for ${\sim}99\%$ of the learned routing signal.

\paragraph{World Model Routing.}
ITP \cite{itp-2026} augments agents with LLM-based world model lookahead, adaptively adjusting the simulation horizon based on task progress.
Dyna-Think \cite{dynathink-2025} integrates world model simulation into the reasoning loop, matching 685B-parameter performance with a 32B model at half the token cost.
Both route to \emph{approximate} world models that inherit LLM hallucination failures.
Our deterministic computation modality provides \emph{exact} state transitions, and our counterfactual analysis reveals that this exactness matters almost exclusively for death avoidance---non-death performance is near-equivalent between modalities.

\paragraph{Agent Frameworks.}
ReAct \cite{react-2023} interleaves reasoning and acting in a single LLM call and serves as a foundational framework for interactive agents including our internal-reasoning baseline.
Our work complements ReAct by analyzing \emph{when} reasoning should yield to deterministic computation and finding that the answer is concentrated in catastrophic failure scenarios.

# Related Work — Draft v1

\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Tool-Use Learning.}
A line of work teaches LLMs when and how to invoke external tools.
Toolformer \cite{toolformer-2024} inserts API calls via self-supervised filtering, while ART \cite{art-2023} uses LLM reasoning chains to select tools automatically, and Chameleon \cite{chameleon-2024} composes diverse tool modules under LLM-as-planner orchestration.
More recently, ReTool \cite{retool-2026} applies reinforcement learning to learn implicit code-interpreter invocation strategies for mathematical reasoning.
Our work differs along three axes: (1) we generate routing labels via \emph{episode-level counterfactual analysis}---running complete trajectories under competing strategies---rather than self-supervised or RL-based signals; (2) we frame routing as \emph{catastrophic failure prevention} rather than general tool selection; and (3) we train an explicit lightweight router decoupled from the backbone LLM, enabling diagnostic analysis of what the routing signal encodes.

\paragraph{Adaptive Computation.}
Several recent methods adapt reasoning effort per step.
CogRouter \cite{cogrouter-2026} achieves 82.3\% on ScienceWorld by routing among cognitive depth levels (instinct to strategic planning) via Cooperative Policy Optimization, while ARES \cite{ares-2026} trains a lightweight router to select per-step reasoning effort (low/medium/high), reducing token cost by 52.7\%.
Mixture-of-Recursions \cite{mixture-of-recursions-2025} applies adaptive depth at the architecture level via per-token recursive routing.
These methods route \emph{how much} to reason; we route \emph{which modality} to use (internal LLM reasoning vs.\ deterministic computation) and contribute the empirical finding that death avoidance accounts for ${\sim}99\%$ of the learned routing signal.

\paragraph{World Model Routing.}
ITP \cite{itp-2026} augments agents with LLM-based world model lookahead, adaptively adjusting the simulation horizon based on task progress.
Dyna-Think \cite{dynathink-2025} integrates world model simulation into the reasoning loop, matching 685B-parameter performance with a 32B model at half the token cost.
Both route to \emph{approximate} world models that inherit LLM hallucination failures.
Our deterministic computation modality provides \emph{exact} state transitions, and our counterfactual analysis reveals that this exactness matters almost exclusively for death avoidance---non-death performance is near-equivalent between modalities.

\paragraph{Agent Frameworks.}
ReAct \cite{react-2023} interleaves reasoning and acting in a single LLM call and serves as a foundational framework for interactive agents including our internal-reasoning baseline.
Our work complements ReAct by analyzing \emph{when} reasoning should yield to deterministic computation and finding that the answer is concentrated in catastrophic failure scenarios.
